title: Universal invariant power lifting makes a free affine quotient affine
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $G$ be a flat affine finitely presented $S$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with group-object diagrams over $S$. Finite presentation means locally finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Assume the following universal power-lifting property. For every commutative $R$-algebra $R'$, every equivariant surjection $E\twoheadrightarrow F$ of arbitrary commutative $R'$-algebras with $G_{R'}$-actions, and every invariant $b\in F^{G_{R'}}$, some $b^N$, $N\geq1$, is the image of an invariant of $E$. Here actions are algebra coactions $\rho:E\to E\otimes_{R'}\Gamma(G_{R'},\mathcal O)$ satisfying counit and coassociativity, invariants satisfy $\rho(e)=e\otimes1$, and equivariance means commuting with coactions. Let $X$ be an affine $S$-scheme with a right $G$-action free on every test $S$-scheme: $xg=x$ implies $g=1$. Form the fppf sheaf quotient $Y=X/G$, the sheafification of right orbits [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Suppose $Y$ is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], $q:X\to Y$ has fppf local sections, and $(x,g)\mapsto(x,xg)$ identifies $X\times_SG$ with $X\times_YX$ as sheaves. Then $Y$ is represented by an affine $S$-scheme, and $q$ is an affine finitely presented morphism. No finite-type hypothesis on $X\to S$ is imposed.

source.place: Alper, Adequate moduli spaces and geometrically reductive group schemes, Proposition 9.7.8, printed p.528, with Lemma 9.2.5(3) and Theorem 4.3.1 (power-lifting formulation of geometric reductivity and the adequate Serre criterion). The assertion that q is affine finitely presented is fppf descent from the trivial torsor projection. WANTED local copy; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale map $h_V\to Y$ from a scheme $V$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Since $q$ has fppf local sections, the point $V\to Y$ lifts to $X$ fppf locally: there are an fppf covering $\{U_i\to V\}$ of schemes [def-pc-fppf-site] and sections $s_i\in X(U_i)$ over the composites $U_i\to Y$. By [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus] (1), (4) and (3), the composites form an fppf family $\{U_i\to Y\}$ of algebraic spaces. The torsor isomorphism gives, for each $T\to U_i$ and $x\in X(T)$ over $T\to U_i\to Y$, a unique $g\in G(T)$ with $x=s_i|_Tg$: apply its inverse to $(s_i|_T,x)\in(X\times_YX)(T)$. Consequently $(u,g)\mapsto(s_i(u)g,u)$, which lies over $Y$ because $q$ is invariant, identifies $U_i\times_SG$ with $X\times_YU_i$. The inverse sends $(x,u)$ to $(u,g)$ using this unique $g$. These formulas commute with all test maps and are mutually inverse, so the identification is an isomorphism of sheaves over $U_i$.

source.place: Proposition 9.7.8: principal homogeneous space hypothesis, explicit local trivialization

proof.text: The identity section makes $G\to S$ surjective; it is flat and locally finitely presented by hypothesis, hence a single fppf covering. By [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus], each $U_i\times_SG\to U_i$ is fppf. Use [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to form $U=\coprod_i U_i$. Its components are disjoint open subschemes. Flatness and local finite presentation are local on these source opens by their local definitions, so $U\to Y$ is flat, locally finitely presented and surjective. The local models of Step 1 glue over these disjoint opens, giving $X\times_YU\simeq U\times_SG$. The projection is flat and locally finitely presented by fppf base change. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-flat-lfp-fppf-descent] to the single surjective cover $U\to Y$: $q$ is flat and locally finitely presented. Its local sections give surjectivity, so $\{q\}$ is itself an fppf cover. The same local models are affine by base change of $G\to S$, using [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent]; descent in that node makes $q$ affine. On every scheme test, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes an affine map quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated. Thus $q$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented, which is precisely finite presentation. All these assertions concern morphisms, and require no finite-type assumption on $X\to S$.

source.place: Fppf locality of affineness and local finite presentation; torsor local models

proof.text: Since $X$ is affine it is quasi-compact, and $q$ is surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-quasicompact-surjection], regarding spaces as discrete stacks, to get quasi-compactness of $Y$. To check quasi-separatedness take the absolute diagonal $\Delta_Y:Y\to Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}Y$. The map $q\times q$ to its target is fppf: factor it as two base changes of $q$ and use [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. Its pullback of $\Delta_Y$ is the map $X\times_YX\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$. The source is $X\times_SG$ and the target is $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$; both are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. A map of affine schemes is the spectrum of its homomorphism of global rings [def-weil-affine-spectrum], hence affine. By [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent] the diagonal $\Delta_Y$ is affine. On affine tests [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact. This is the quasi-separatedness of $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 9.7.8: qcqs prerequisite for Theorem 4.3.1, verified by the affine torsor relation

proof.text: Take any surjection $\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ of arbitrary quasi-coherent commutative algebras on $Y$, and $c\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal C)$. By [lem-sfb-affine-torsor-algebra-invariants] and Step 2 it pulls back to an equivariant surjection $E_{\mathcal B}\twoheadrightarrow E_{\mathcal C}$ of $R$-algebras, with $c$ corresponding to an invariant $\bar c$. Apply the assumed universal power-lifting property with $R'=R$: obtain $N>0$ and $e\in E_{\mathcal B}^G$ mapping to $\bar c^N$. The natural invariant-section isomorphisms in the cited node give a section $b\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal B)$ whose image is $c^N$. The algebras quantified over here need not have finite type or descend from the base. Thus $Y$ has the global algebra-surjection power-lifting property.

source.place: Proposition 9.7.8, power-lifting argument underlying Theorem 9.1.4 and Lemma 9.2.5(3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-power-lifting-affineness] to $Y/S$: Step 3 gives both required compactness conditions and Step 4 gives power lifting for every quasi-coherent algebra surjection. Hence $Y$ is represented by an affine scheme. Its given structure map to $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a map between affine schemes, so it is affine by the spectrum description [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. This proves the asserted affine $S$-representability; the affine finite-presentation assertion for $q$ was established in Step 2.
